column1: abasement§Years of self-abasement had left him unable to argue for a raise.§多年的自我**贬抑**让他连要求加薪都开不了口。
abate§The fever abated by morning and she asked for breakfast.§到早晨烧就**退了**，她要了早饭。
abbreviate§Please do not abbreviate the author's name in the citation.§引文中请不要**缩写**作者姓名。
aberration§One bad quarter is an aberration; four is a pattern.§一个糟糕的季度是**反常**，四个就是规律了。
abhor§Nature abhors a vacuum, and so does a committee agenda.§自然**厌恶**真空，委员会的议程也一样。
abhorrence§Their shared abhorrence of waste held the household together.§对浪费共同的**痛恨**维系着这个家。
abound§Rumors abounded in the week before the announcement was made.§宣布前的那一周，谣言**满天飞**。
abridge§No one may abridge a right that the charter guarantees.§任何人都不得**剥夺**宪章所保障的权利。
abridgment§Students read the abridgment; scholars read all nine volumes.§学生读**删节本**，学者读全部九卷。
abruptness§There was an abruptness in her manner that visitors mistook for rudeness.§她举止里有一种**唐突**，客人常误以为是粗鲁。
absolutist§His absolutist reading of the rule left no room for judgment.§他对规则**绝对化**的理解不留任何判断余地。
absolve§Signing the waiver does not absolve the organizers of responsibility.§签署免责书并不**免除**组织者的责任。
abstain§He abstains from coffee after four in the afternoon.§下午四点以后他就**不喝咖啡**了。
abstemious§An abstemious month after the holidays became a lifelong habit.§假期后**节制的**一个月变成了终身的习惯。
abstinence§The pledge of abstinence lasted until the first cold evening.§**戒酒**的誓言持续到第一个寒冷的夜晚为止。
abstraction§He works in abstraction and leaves the fieldwork to others.§他做**抽象研究**，把田野工作留给别人。
abstruse§What seems abstruse in the first chapter is plain by the fourth.§第一章看似**深奥的**东西，到第四章就明白了。
absurdity§She pointed out the absurdity without ever raising her voice.§她指出其中的**荒谬**，却从未提高嗓门。
accentuate§A pause before the last word accentuates it better than volume.§在最后一个词前停顿，比加大音量更能**强调**它。
acceptance§Acceptance of the terms is implied by continued use.§继续使用即视为**接受**这些条款。
accidental§An accidental spill on the negative produced the effect he spent years copying.§底片上一次**意外的**泼溅造就了他花多年模仿的效果。
acclaim§Audiences acclaimed the ending that critics had dismissed.§观众为评论家所否定的结局**叫好**。
acclamation§He was elected by acclamation and served for eleven years.§他以**欢呼**推举当选，任职十一年。
accommodate§The timetable was changed to accommodate the night shift.§时刻表作了改动以**照顾**夜班工人。
accomplishment§Speaking four languages was the least of her accomplishments.§会说四种语言是她**成就**中最微不足道的一项。
accost§She was accosted by a photographer as she left the courtroom.§她走出法庭时被一名摄影师**拦住搭话**。
accusation§He answered the accusation with a receipt and a date.§他用一张收据和一个日期回应了这项**指控**。
acquiesce§Do not acquiesce in a decision you will have to defend later.§不要**默许**一个你日后还得为它辩护的决定。
acquiescent§Years of acquiescent silence had made the abuse routine.§多年**顺从的**沉默使这种欺压变成了常态。
acquisitive§An acquisitive age fills its houses and empties its attics.§**贪求占有**的时代把房子塞满，把阁楼掏空。
acrid§An acrid remark from the back row ended the discussion.§后排一句**尖刻的**话结束了讨论。
acrimony§The divorce was concluded without acrimony, which surprised the lawyers.§这场离婚没有**恶言相向**就结束了，律师们很意外。
acronym§Every department invented an acronym nobody outside it understood.§每个部门都造了一个外人听不懂的**缩写词**。
acumen§Political acumen is knowing which fight to lose.§政治上的**敏锐**，就是知道该输掉哪一场仗。
adamant§Diamond is adamant, which is exactly where the word comes from.§金刚石**极为坚硬**，这个词正是由此而来。
adaptable§An adaptable design outlives a perfect one.§**适应性强**的设计比完美的设计活得更久。
adept§He became adept at reading handwriting three centuries old.§他变得很**擅长**辨认三百年前的手写体。
ad-lib§Her ad-lib answer was quoted more often than the prepared speech.§她**即兴**的回答被引用得比准备好的演讲还多。
administer§Nurses administer the dose; the pharmacist calculates it.§护士**给药**，药剂师负责计算剂量。
administrator§A good administrator is noticed only when she leaves.§好的**管理者**只有在离开时才被察觉。
admonition§The sign carried a single admonition: close the gate.§牌子上只有一句**告诫**：请关门。
adorn§She adorned the letter with nothing but a date and a signature.§她给这封信只**添了**一个日期和一个签名。
adroit§An adroit change of subject saved the dinner.§一次**机敏**的话题转换救了这顿晚餐。
adulation§Adulation is harder to survive than criticism.§**奉承**比批评更难熬过去。
adulatory§He wrote an adulatory preface and a scathing private letter.§他写了一篇**奉承的**序言，又写了一封尖刻的私信。
advancement§The advancement of the science owed as much to accident as to design.§这门科学的**进步**既靠设计，也靠偶然。
advantageous§The wind was advantageous, and they reached port a day early.§风向**有利**，他们提前一天到港。
adversary§A good adversary makes you rewrite your own argument.§好的**对手**会逼你重写自己的论证。
adversity§He wrote his best work in adversity and his worst in comfort.§他在**逆境**中写出最好的作品，在安逸中写出最差的。
aerate§Rain aerates the lawn more effectively than any machine.§雨水给草坪**通气**比任何机器都有效。
aesthetic§The aesthetic of the whole issue is set by its margins.§整期刊物的**审美**由页边距决定。
affability§Her affability was professional, and none the worse for it.§她的**和蔼**是职业性的，但并不因此逊色。
affable§He remained affable through four hours of hostile questions.§四小时的敌意提问里，他始终**和蔼**。
affiliation§He listed no political affiliation on the form.§他在表格上没有填写任何**政治派别**。
affliction§Drought is an affliction the region has learned to plan around.§干旱是这个地区已经学会预先应对的**苦难**。
affluence§Affluence arrived with the railway and left with the mill.§**富裕**随铁路而来，随磨坊而去。
affordable§Nothing on the menu was affordable on a student's budget.§菜单上没有一样是学生预算**负担得起**的。
agent§Salt is the agent that does the damage, not the water itself.§**造成损害的**是盐，而不是水本身。
aggrandize§The wing was built to aggrandize the family, not to house books.§这座侧翼是为**抬高家族声望**而建，不是为了藏书。
aggregation§An aggregation of small errors is harder to find than one large one.§**一堆小错误**比一个大错误更难查出。
agile§An agile mind is not the same as a quick one.§头脑**灵活**与头脑快不是一回事。
agitate§The mixture must be agitated for a full minute.§这种混合物必须**搅动**整整一分钟。
agitation§The lake showed no agitation, and the search went on until dark.§湖面毫无**波动**，搜寻一直持续到天黑。
agnostic§On the question of the second author she remained agnostic.§关于第二作者是谁的问题，她始终**不下判断**。
agreeable§He was agreeable to every suggestion except the one that mattered.§除了那条要紧的，他对每条建议都**同意**。
alacrity§The crew turned out with alacrity at two in the morning.§凌晨两点，船员们**迅速**集合。
allege§Nothing alleged in the letter could be checked against a record.§信中所**声称**的一切都无从与记录核对。
alleviate§An extra staircase would alleviate the crush at closing time.§多一道楼梯就能**缓解**闭馆时的拥挤。
